title: Patient Accounting Standard: Entering the Patient Payment Plans Add-On Fee by Financial Class
content:
How the scheduled add-on fee on a Patient Payment Plans plan becomes the fee entered on the plan balance follows the financial class of the patient's Patient Financial Account. The scheduled add-on fee is the add-on fee owed before it is entered, carried unrounded.

**Standard.**

1. On the High-Deductible Health Plan Account the scheduled add-on fee is rounded down to the whole dollar.
2. On the Self-Pay Account it is rounded down to the half dollar.
3. On every other class it is rounded half up to the cent.

| Financial class of the Patient Financial Account | Fee entered | Scheduled 17.28 | Scheduled 5.40 |
|---|---|---|---|
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account | Rounded down to the whole dollar | 17.00 | 5.00 |
| Self-Pay Account | Rounded down to the half dollar | 17.00 | 5.00 |
| Medicaid Managed Care, Medicare Part B, Medicare Advantage, Commercial HMO/EPO or Commercial PPO/POS Account | Rounded half up to the cent | 17.28 | 5.40 |

**Terms.** Rounding down to the half dollar takes the fee to the nearest 0.50 step at or below it: 17.28 becomes 17.00 and 17.64 becomes 17.50. Rounding down to the whole dollar drops any cents: 17.64 becomes 17.00.
